speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; please describe exactly where it is located and how long it has been there. Additionally, what does the wound look like, and do you have any fever or other medical conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent uveitis, are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications or steroids? Also, is the leg lesion warm to the touch, and is there any drainage?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (likely *Leishmania braziliensis* or similar) with secondary infection or superinfection, given the central necrosis, irregular purplish borders, history of insect bite, and underlying immunosuppression from Crohn's disease, diabetes, and prior steroid use.
